audiences.heading: Two ways North Dakota lets this course help you
audiences.intro: Both use the same course. They work differently, and only one of them can be used in any twelve-month period.

items.label: Points on your record
items.heading: Take three points off, once every twelve months
items.body: Complete an approved course and NDDOT reduces your accumulated points by three. Once every twelve months, up to nine points in any three-year period. The reduction applies only to points that were on your record before you finished the course.

items.label: Just got a ticket
items.heading: Keep the points off entirely
items.body: For a violation worth five points or fewer, you can elect at court, when you post bond, to take an approved course instead of having the points entered. The bond is still forfeited. NDDOT must receive your certificate within 30 days of the election, and using this option means no three-point reduction that year.

items.label: Near suspension
items.heading: Twelve points is a suspension. The course does not undo it.
items.body: At twelve or more points (six for a driver under 18) North Dakota suspends the license, seven days for every point over eleven. If you are already there, the three-point reduction applies only after the suspension is served. The course still helps; it just does not skip the suspension.

benefits.headline: A three-point reduction, once every twelve months
benefits.body: North Dakota Century Code 39-06.1-13(2) lets the director reduce a driver's accumulated points by three on completion of an approved course, once in any twelve-month period and no more than nine points in any three-year period. The reduction applies to points accumulated before completion.

benefits.headline: A course in lieu of points for small violations
benefits.body: Under NDCC 39-06.1-10.1 a cited driver may elect at court, when posting bond, to complete an approved course instead of having the points entered. Available for violations carrying five points or fewer, once every twelve months. The bond is forfeited, and proof of completion must reach NDDOT within thirty days.

benefits.headline: A certificate you send to NDDOT yourself
benefits.body: North Dakota has no provider reporting system. You receive a certificate on completion and deliver it to the Driver License Division by email or mail. NDDOT applies the reduction to your record.

faqs.q: How many points does the course take off?
faqs.a: Three, once every twelve months, capped at nine points in any three-year period. The reduction applies to points that were on your record before you completed the course, not to points added later.

A choice you make at court when you post bond for a violation worth five points or fewer: complete an approved course and the points are never entered on your record. The bond is still forfeited. You must get your certificate to NDDOT within 30 days of the election, and you can only use the option once every twelve months. It is not a dismissal.

faqs.q: Can I use both the reduction and the in-lieu option in the same year?
faqs.a: No. Electing a course in lieu of points forfeits the three-point reduction for that twelve-month period.

faqs.q: I have twelve points. Will the course stop my suspension?
faqs.a: No. At twelve or more points North Dakota suspends the license, seven days for each point over eleven. The reduction applies only after the suspension is served. Take the course anyway so the reduction is ready when you are eligible.

faqs.q: How long does the course take?
faqs.a: Four hours, self-paced. Most people finish in one or two evenings. There is no state deadline for the course itself; only the in-lieu election carries a 30-day submission deadline.

faqs.q: What is the final exam like?
faqs.a: Twenty-five questions, eighteen correct to pass. Unlimited retakes with different questions and no waiting period.

faqs.q: How do I get my certificate to NDDOT?
faqs.a: Email it to drs@nd.gov or mail it to the Driver License Division. We attach the instructions to your certificate email. North Dakota has no provider reporting system, so this step is yours.

faqs.q: Can I do this on my phone?
